assessment.reason: Charbonnet is set to debut off a torn ACL, but his snap plan and Price's possible activation are unresolved. The model has no 2026 sample, so the over depends on an assumed prior-style receiving role that a managed debut could undercut.
assessment.model_case: Projection of 1.72 receptions sits just above 1.5, with a wide spread. It uses zero current-season weight, built on about 2.1 targets and a high catch rate from prior history. Defense and venue add only a small amount, so the case rests on that inherited role, not on adjustments. Raw-to-calibrated moves only slightly.
assessment.price_case: Main line, not an alternate: all five books sit at 1.5. BetMGM's +155 is the best price; four others are +134 to +139. Break-even at +155 is far below the model's figure but near de-vigged consensus. The gap reflects a price outlier at one book, not a different expected outcome.
assessment.context_case: Reporting confirms planned participation and a crowded backfield. It does not describe his snap or route share for a first game back. Price's roster status is undecided until Monday.
blocking_checks: Whether Jadarian Price is activated Monday afternoon; another back would cut into Charbonnet's passing-down snaps.
Any reported snap or rep plan for Charbonnet's ACL return; a capped workload would likely push expected catches below 1.5.

qualitative_review.countercase: With Walker gone, Charbonnet could slide into a larger all-purpose role than last year. Left tackle Charles Cross being out could also push quick throws and checkdowns to backs. Either would support the prior-history target rate even in a debut. If Price stays on IR and Charbonnet takes passing downs, +155 looks generous versus a +134 to +139 field.
open_checks: Reconfirm BetMGM still offers +155 at 1.5 before the 8:20 PM EST kickoff Monday.
Check final inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff for Price and the running back group.
Gauge how Cross's absence shifts protection duties and checkdown volume for backs.

findings.note: Bears team preview: Caleb Williams has thrown for 300+ yards with no interceptions in back-to-back starts, Chicago leads the NFL in rushing at 154.3 yards per game, and Seattle gets RBs Charbonnet and Price back. It also says Simmons, Sweat and Edwards strengthen Chicago's defense.

Seattle's final injury report has LT Charles Cross, WR Rashid Shaheed and RB Velus Jones Jr. out and OLB Nwosu doubtful. Chicago lists only RB Monangai as out, which fits a less explosive Seattle offense.

CBS/SportsLine lists Seattle -3 with a total of 46.5, the same as the bet's line. The page says its model has an over/under pick, but the retrieved snippet doesn't show which side, and it notes Bears TE Cole Kmet is out for the season.

Covers lists D'Andre Swift Over 3.5 receptions as part of a combo bet, but the pick assumes Kyle Monangai is out and a negative game script, and its call of a third straight 4+ catch game depends on TE Colston Loveland sitting, whose status was not confirmed.

The Bears' official preview says backup RB Kyle Monangai will miss a fourth straight game with a toe injury, which keeps Swift as the lead back. Swift has 116 carries for 476 yards and 7 TDs, and Seattle's pass defense ranks No. 1.

Covers says Chicago, a 3-point underdog, may shift volume toward Burden, Loveland and Odunze if Seattle leads, which could cut Swift's targets. It also says Seattle's linebackers are vulnerable to backs as receivers and that Swift played 86% of snaps in Week 7.
